headline: Energy Stands Alone as Friday's Tape Tilts Lower, With Gulf Tensions Framing the Week
body_html:
Wall Street closed the week on Friday, October 23, with losers well ahead of winners. Of the 544 stocks we track, 340 fell and 198 rose. Energy was the one clear bright spot, gaining 2.63%, while consumer names lagged with a 1.59% drop and materials slid 0.87%.

Individual stories mattered more than sector direction. Robert Half surged 21.74%, and cybersecurity names found buyers, with CrowdStrike up 8.25% and Zscaler up 7.31%. Tidewater added 8.11% in oil services. On the other side, Corcept Therapeutics tumbled 20.13%, Bloom Energy fell 11.24%, Credo Technology lost 9.51% and Comfort Systems USA gave up 9.26%. Semiconductors edged up 0.18% while software slipped 0.11%.

Looking to Monday, October 26, traders will watch the Middle East. Saudi Arabia reports intercepting drones and missiles as fighting with Yemen's Houthis continues, and Iran says it downed a US drone. Iran's president has also urged a fresh try at an interim deal. Worries over AI funding are another thread investors will keep weighing.

briefs.headline: Energy Takes the Top Spot
briefs.body: Energy was the only group with a meaningful gain on Friday, up 2.63%, and Tidewater rose 8.11%. Reports of Houthi claims against Saudi oil sites and fighting in the region form the backdrop. Traders will see whether the strength carries into Monday.

briefs.headline: Security Software Catches a Bid
briefs.body: CrowdStrike climbed 8.25% and Zscaler rose 7.31%, even as the broader software group slipped 0.11%. The split shows buyers favoring cybersecurity over the wider category. Investors will look for follow-through when trading resumes on Monday, October 26.

briefs.headline: Staffing Firm Delivers the Session's Biggest Pop
briefs.body: Robert Half jumped 21.74%, the largest gain among the stocks we track on Friday. The move stood out in a session where industrials as a group fell 0.43%. It was a company-specific surge, not a sign of a sector-wide rally.

briefs.headline: Biotech Splits Sharply
briefs.body: Genmab rose 9.47%, but Corcept Therapeutics plunged 20.13%, the steepest drop in our universe on Friday. Healthcare as a whole fell 0.61%. The gap between the two shows how much single-stock news is driving the sector.

briefs.headline: AI-Linked Names Stumble Amid Funding Worries
briefs.body: Credo Technology dropped 9.51%, Bloom Energy 11.24% and Comfort Systems USA 9.26%. This came as commentary on AI funding fears circulated. Semiconductors still edged up 0.18%, so the pressure was uneven across the theme.

briefs.headline: Consumer Weakness Hides an Auto-Supplier Divide
briefs.body: Consumer shares were the weakest group, down 1.59%. Auto suppliers moved in opposite directions: Gentherm gained 9.37% while Visteon fell 6.52%. With winter nearing, heating oil costs are also emerging as a political issue in US Senate races.
